## What Are We Building?

::: {.incremental}
- An **MCP (Model Context Protocol) server** that lets an AI assistant answer questions about Swedish solar power
- Combines **two real data sources**: historical installation stats + live weather forecasts
- Deployed on **Azure**, connected to **Microsoft Copilot Studio**
- You can ask things like:
  - *"How fast has solar grown in Karlskrona?"*
  - *"How much power will clouds cost us this week?"*
  - *"Which Swedish city will generate the most solar electricity next week?"*
  - *"Show me a map of solar capacity across Sweden"*
:::

## Why Does This Matter?

Sweden's installed solar capacity has grown **35×** in eight years:

| Year | National Installed Capacity |
|------|----------------------------|
| 2016 | 134 MW |
| 2019 | 691 MW |
| 2021 | 1,578 MW |
| 2023 | 3,962 MW |
| **2024** | **4,808 MW** |

::: {.callout-note}
**56% CAGR since 2016.** With growth this fast, planners, grid operators, and investors need real-time answers — not static reports.
:::

## The Idea: Natural Language → Data

Instead of:
> "Go to the Energimyndigheten website, download the Excel, filter by municipality, cross-reference with the SMHI API for weather..."

Just ask:
> *"How much solar power will Göteborg lose to clouds this week, compared to a clear-sky scenario?"*

MCP is the **bridge** that makes this possible.

## What is MCP?

```
User in Copilot Studio
       │
       │  Natural language question
       ▼
  Copilot Studio (AI)           ← decides which tool to call
       │
       │  POST /mcp  (Streamable HTTP)
       ▼
  MCP Server (our code)         ← executes the tool,
       │                           returns structured data + images
       │  JSON + base64 PNG
       ▼
  Copilot Studio (AI)           ← formats as natural language
       │
       ▼
  User gets a clear answer
```

MCP = **standardised protocol** for AI ↔ tool communication (open standard, March 2025)

## Architecture

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    CS["Copilot Studio\n(Client)"] -->|Streamable HTTP\nPOST /mcp| ACA["Azure Container App\nFastAPI + MCP Server"]
    ACA -->|parquet on disk| EM["Energimyndigheten\n290 municipalities\n2016–2024"]
    ACA -->|live REST API| SMHI["SMHI Open Data\n9-day point forecast\n30-min cache"]
    EM --> ACA
    SMHI --> ACA
```

**4 tools exposed:**

| Tool | Data source |
|------|------------|
| `get_solar_growth` | Energimyndigheten (static) |
| `compare_generation_forecast` | SMHI (live) |
| `find_optimal_solar_region` | Both |
| `get_solar_map` | Both — returns PNG image |

## Data Source 1: Energimyndigheten

**Swedish Energy Agency — Grid-connected solar installations**

- PxWeb API: `pxexternal.energimyndigheten.se`
- Dataset: *Nätanslutna solcellsanläggningar* (EN0123)
- **290 municipalities × 9 years (2016–2024)**
- Downloaded and cached as Parquet (~2,600 rows)

**Schema:**

| Column | Example |
|--------|---------|
| `municipality` | Karlskrona |
| `municipality_code` | 0680 |
| `year` | 2024 |
| `num_installations` | 3,293 |
| `capacity_kw` | 54,810 kW |

## Data Source 2: SMHI Open Data

**Swedish Meteorological and Hydrological Institute**

- Free API, CC BY 4.0 — no API key needed
- Endpoint: `opendata-download-metfcst.smhi.se/api/category/pmp3g/version/2`
- **9-day point forecast** (~80 time steps, hourly then 3-hourly)

**Key parameters we use:**

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `lcc_mean` | Low cloud cover (0–8 oktas) — blocks ~90% of solar |
| `mcc_mean` | Mid cloud cover (0–8 oktas) — blocks ~70% |
| `hcc_mean` | High cloud cover (0–8 oktas) — blocks ~30% (thin cirrus) |
| `Wsymb2` | Weather symbol (fallback) |

::: {.callout-tip}
**30-minute in-memory cache** — one SMHI call per city per 30 min, regardless of how many users ask.
:::

## Solar Generation Formula

```
Energy (kWh) = Capacity (kW) × Clearness × Peak_Sun_Hours × PR
```

**Clearness index** from weighted cloud layers (0 = full overcast, 1 = clear sky):

```python
clearness = 1.0 - 0.95 × (0.9×lcc + 0.7×mcc + 0.3×hcc) / 8
```

**Clear-sky Peak Sun Hours** by latitude and month (PVGIS):

| Latitude | Jan | Feb | Jun | Aug |
|----------|-----|-----|-----|-----|
| 55°N (Malmö) | 1.2 h | 2.3 h | 8.4 h | 6.8 h |
| 59°N (Stockholm) | 0.8 h | 1.9 h | 8.2 h | 6.4 h |
| 66°N (Luleå) | 0.2 h | 1.1 h | 7.7 h | 5.7 h |

**Performance Ratio (PR) = 0.80** — inverter losses, wiring, temperature.

## Tool 2: `compare_generation_forecast`

> *"How much power will Karlskrona lose to clouds this week?"*

```json
{
  "municipality": "Karlskrona",
  "installed_capacity_kw": 54810,
  "days_ahead": 7,
  "avg_clearness_index": 0.21,
  "forecast_energy_kwh": 14200,
  "clear_sky_energy_kwh": 67600,
  "cloud_loss_kwh": 53400,
  "cloud_loss_pct": 79.0,
  "dominant_weather": "Variable cloudiness",
  "summary": "Over the next 7 days, Karlskrona is forecast to generate
    ~14,200 kWh. Under perfectly clear skies it would generate 67,600 kWh
    — clouds reduce potential generation by 79% in February."
}
```

::: {.callout-tip}
February at 56°N: only ~2.3 clear-sky peak sun hours per day — winter losses are expected.
:::

  },

## Tool 4: `get_solar_map`

> *"Show me a map of installed solar capacity across Sweden"*

Returns two things:

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**JSON summary:**
```json
{
  "year": 2024,
  "total_capacity_mw": 4808,
  "municipalities_with_data": 290,
  "top_10_municipalities": [
    {"municipality": "Göteborg",
     "capacity_kw": 164520},
    ...
  ]
}
```
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**PNG choropleth map:**
- Sweden coloured by installed kW
- YlOrRd scale (yellow → red)
- Grey = no data
- Generated via folium + Playwright
- ~85 KB base64 PNG via `ImageContent`
:::
:::

## The Generation Logic — Explained

**Why does Göteborg generate more than Gotland despite being cloudier?**

| | Gotland | Göteborg |
|--|---------|---------|
| Clearness index | 0.34 | 0.20 |
| Capacity (kW) | 38,460 | 164,520 |
| PSH Feb (h/day) | 2.1 | 2.0 |
| **Forecast kWh** | **9,200** | **48,200** |

$$
\text{kWh} = \underbrace{164{,}520}_{\text{capacity}} \times \underbrace{0.20}_{\text{clearness}} \times \underbrace{2.0}_{\text{PSH}} \times 7 \times \underbrace{0.80}_{\text{PR}} = 48{,}200
$$

Capacity wins — every time.

## Server Code (FastAPI + MCP)

```python
from mcp.server import Server
from mcp.server.streamable_http_manager import StreamableHTTPSessionManager
from mcp.types import ImageContent, TextContent, Tool

mcp_server = Server("solar-sweden-mcp")
app = FastAPI(lifespan=_lifespan)

# Streamable HTTP — Copilot Studio connects here
app.mount("/mcp", _MCPStreamableHTTPApp())

@mcp_server.list_tools()
async def list_tools() -> list[Tool]:
    return [solar_growth_tool, forecast_tool,
            optimal_region_tool, solar_map_tool]

@mcp_server.call_tool()
async def call_tool(name, arguments) -> list[TextContent | ImageContent]:
    ...  # routes to the right tool function
```

::: {.callout-note}
**SSE fallback** at `/sse` for older MCP clients. Both transports run simultaneously.
:::

## Azure Deployment

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.12-slim
RUN apt-get install -y libglib2.0-0 libnss3 libatk1.0-0 \
    libxcb1 libgbm1 libpango-1.0-0 libcairo2  # Playwright deps

RUN pip install -r requirements.txt
RUN playwright install chromium          # for map screenshots

COPY src/ ./src/
COPY data/ ./data/                       # parquet + geojson baked in

EXPOSE 8000
CMD ["uvicorn", "solar_mcp.server:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]
```

**Azure setup:**
1. `az acr build` → push image (~1.2 GB with Chromium)
2. `az containerapp create` → deploy with scale-to-zero
3. Register `https://<app>.azurecontainerapps.io/mcp` in Copilot Studio
